title: Aztec Eagle and Jaguar Warriors
hook: To join elite orders, warriors had to capture four enemy soldiers alive.

scenes.text: In the Aztec army, hereditary birth did not guarantee military status: true honor had to be earned on the field of combat.
scenes.imagePrompt: Stone ceremonial courtyard of the Aztec temple of the Eagle and Jaguar warriors in Malinalco with carved rock portals. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: In the Aztec army, hereditary birth did not guarantee military status: true honor had to be earned on the field of combat.

scenes.text: To join the elite warrior fraternities—the Eagle and Jaguar societies—a soldier had to capture four enemy champions alive in single combat.
scenes.imagePrompt: Quilted cotton ichcahuipilli armor suit soaked in brine for toughness displayed on a wooden armor stand in temple light. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: To join the elite warrior fraternities—the Eagle and Jaguar societies—a soldier had to capture four enemy champions alive in single combat.

scenes.text: Jaguar warriors wore full-body battle suits tailored from real spotted jaguar pelts, with their faces peering out from the snarling open jaw.

scenes.voicedText: Jaguar warriors wore full-body battle suits tailored from real spotted jaguar pelts, with their faces peering out from the snarling open jaw.

scenes.text: Eagle warriors wore helmets shaped like curved raptor beaks, adorned with thousands of iridescent green quetzal and eagle feathers.
